original_statement: Anonymous drivers stay anonymous end to end: no signer identity in UI state, logs, or ordering.
restatement: When a driver declares an anonymous membership model, nothing the client retains or displays can be traced back to which member signed what. Anonymity is a property of the client's own state, not of its rendering — the identity must be absent, not merely unshown. (s1) UI-observable state carries only n-of-m slot counts, with no field naming or distinguishing which member filled which slot; (s2) no log record on any path, including debug, error, and crash paths, contains a signer identifier or a value resolving to one; (s3) the order contributions appear in UI state and in the log depends on arrival and log position only, never on who signed them; (s4) the client's logical timing — the sequence and content of emitted state-update events — is independent of signer identity; (s5) no client-held artifact at all (log, reduced state, cache, crash dump, export) contains a path back to a signer identity.

restatement_clauses.text: UI state exposes counts, never identities. For an anonymous driver, the state the UI can observe carries only n-of-m slots filled — no field anywhere in UI-reachable state names or distinguishes which member filled which slot.
Local logs carry no signer identity. At every level and on every path — including debug, error, and crash paths — no log record contains a signer identifier or any value that resolves to one.

Ordering leaks nothing. The order contributions appear in UI state and in the log is independent of who signed them: permuting the signers across the same set of contributions produces the same observable ordering.

Logical timing leaks nothing. The sequence and content of emitted state-update events — logical clock values, event ordering, batching boundaries — are independent of signer identity. This is scoped to what the client controls and makes no wall-clock side-channel claim.
Anonymity covers everything retained, not just what's shown. No client-held artifact — log, reduced state, cache, crash dump, or export — contains a path back to a signer identity.

goal: For an anonymous-membership driver, no client-held state, log, ordering, or retained artifact can be traced back to which member signed what — identity is absent from the client, not merely unrendered.

acceptance_tests.proves: Across the explored space of signer-to-slot assignments over a fixed set of contributions, the UI-observable state matches the baseline at every reachable assignment. An identity that reached UI state — including one a component merely declines to render — diverges under some permutation, so this pins 'absent' rather than 'unshown' over the whole assignment space.
acceptance_tests.description: UI state exposes counts, never identities. For an anonymous driver, the state the UI can observe carries only n-of-m slots filled — no field anywhere in UI-reachable state names or distinguishes which member filled which slot.

acceptance_tests.proves: Across the reachable logging state space (debug, info, warn, error, verification-failure, crash, shutdown), no emitted record contains a signer identifier or a value resolving to one — catching the error-path log line that names a signer while the happy path stays clean.
acceptance_tests.description: Local logs carry no signer identity. At every level and on every path — including debug, error, and crash paths — no log record contains a signer identifier or any value that resolves to one.

acceptance_tests.proves: Over all explored delivery interleavings (varied arrival orders, signers, duplicates, retries), the observable order is a function of arrival and log position only and never of signer — catching a reducer that sorts or buckets by signer key, quantified over interleavings rather than a single permutation pair.
acceptance_tests.description: Ordering leaks nothing. The order contributions appear in UI state and in the log is independent of who signed them: permuting the signers across the same set of contributions produces the same observable ordering.

acceptance_tests.proves: Across the explored space of signer assignments crossed with delivery batching, the sequence and content of emitted state-update events — logical clock values, event ordering, batching boundaries — matches the baseline at every reachable state, with no wall clock measured. Catches a client that coalesces or defers updates differently per signer, while making no wall-clock side-channel claim the oracle could not honestly enforce.
acceptance_tests.description: Logical timing leaks nothing. The sequence and content of emitted state-update events — logical clock values, event ordering, batching boundaries — are independent of signer identity. This is scoped to what the client controls and makes no wall-clock side-channel claim.

acceptance_tests.proves: The stepper enumerates every retained record type x field across the whole declared retention schema — log records, reduced-state records, cache entries, export format, crash dumps — and no reachable field is identity-derived while every signature-valued field is typed anonymity-set-wide (ring or blind) rather than member-bound. Coverage is the ENTIRE declared schema, not a sampled run: a byte-comparison oracle cannot do this job here, because signature values differ per run even for the same signer set, so permutation equivalence would fail on a correct implementation and any relaxation of it passes vacuously. (Authored as model_check rather than the confirmed proof_obligation because exo-178's authoring gate parses a postcondition in isolation, which admits only closed formulas whose truth no implementation can affect — see this spec's commit message.)
